zh: 好，各位下午好。我是 Brian Kennedy，在 ZoomInfo 的 Agent 平台做工程。我想先给大家看一段我们自己的 Agent 写的东西。这是产品里实际产生的一段输出。
en: BRIAN KENNEDY, All right. Good afternoon, everybody. I am Brian Kennedy. I'm an engineer on ZoomInfo's agentic platform. Now, I want to start with showing you something one of our agents wrote. This is a real output from our product.

zh: Agent 的任务是给一位客户安排一封邮件。这就是它报回来的结果。它说邮件已经安排好了，已经放进发送队列，会在周二发出去。
en: The agent's job was to schedule an email for a customer. And this is what it reported back. It said it scheduled the email, it queued it up, and that it was going to go out on Tuesday.

zh: 我们也会让第二个模型检查 Agent 的工作。我把它叫作裁判。裁判读完后，批准了。好极了。问题来了。这里是实际发生的事。这些是工具的返回结果，记录了 Agent 调用工具时究竟执行了什么。我把这些记录叫作凭据。Agent 试图在 Salesforce 里建一条记录，但失败了。返回的错误消息明确说记录没有建成，还告诉 Agent 别报告成功，也别编造记录。
en: We don't just trust the agent, though. A second model checks the agent's work. I'm going to call this one the judge. The judge read this and it accepted it. Great. Now, here's the problem. And this is what had actually happened. These are the tool results, the record of what actually ran when the agent called the tools. I'm going to call these the receipts. The agent tried to create a record in Salesforce and it failed. The error message that came back says the record was not created and it tells the agent not to report a success or even make up a record.

zh: 这条错误消息正是我们针对这种情况自己写的。Agent 又试了一次，这回建了一个任务，也就是一条待办。邮件从头到尾都没有被安排发送。Agent 手头甚至没有发邮件的工具。它编了个结果，裁判还批准了。这里有两处失败。Agent 编造了一次发送，裁判照章盖了个戳，实际没核查这项说法就批准了。如果你也开发 Agent，大概遇见过这种事，手头也可能有这么一个裁判。它可以是代码审查模型、评测打分模型，也可以是运行循环里的监督者。
en: We wrote this message ourselves for exactly this situation. The agent tried again. It created a task, which is a to-do. No email was ever scheduled. The agent doesn't even have a tool that can send an email. The agent made it up and the judge approved it. So that's two failures. The agent fabricated a send and the judge rubber stamped it, approved a claim that never actually checked. So if you build agents, you probably have run into this and you probably have a judge like this. It might be a code reviewer or a grader of your evals or a supervisor in your

zh: 只要由一个模型来判断另一个模型做得好不好，这种事就有可能发生。接下来十分钟，我会讲我们怎么发现它，又是怎么处理的。先简单交代一下背景。
en: loop. Any time a model decides whether another model's work is good, this can happen. But for For the next 10 minutes, I'll show you how we caught this and what we did about it. First, some quick background.

zh: 我在 ZoomInfo 的团队叫 AgentTeams。我们上周宣布了这个产品。它是 ZoomInfo GTM Studio 里的多 Agent 编排层，让一组各有所长的 Agent 跨多个企业系统协作，执行市场拓展（GTM）流程。
en: My team at ZoomInfo is called AgentTeams. We announced this last week. It's a multi-agent orchestration layer that lives in ZoomInfo's GTM studio. It coordinates a team of specialized agents across a company's systems to run GTM workflows.

zh: 比如找目标公司、调查这些公司、写邮件，再把它记进 CRM。每个 Agent 有自己的角色、指令和工具，比如 Salesforce、HubSpot 和 Slack。这些 Agent 会在客户系统里做真正的决定、采取真正的行动。它们会写入记录，也会发送消息。团队中每个 Agent 每做完一个步骤，就由第二个模型检查。这就是裁判。它有三个选项。继续、重做这一步，或者整个任务到此为止。大家可能听过“用大模型当裁判”这个说法。它跟代码审查模型或评测打分模型是同一个思路。
en: For example, find companies, research them, write an email, log it into their CRM. its own roles and instructions and tools like Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack. These agents make real decisions and take real actions in a customer's systems. They write records and they send messages. Every team and every agent finishes a step. A second model checks its work. That's the judge. And it has three options to move on, to redo the step, or to stop the job altogether. You've probably heard this called LLM as a judge. It's the same idea

zh: 对我们来说，难处在于只有一个模型，却得给所有交到它手里的 Agent 打分。客户可以自行搭建流程，以任何顺序使用任意 Agent 和任意工具，组合几乎无穷无尽。裁判要处理的任务种类也会随之增加。它能看出工作像不像做完了，可它判断不了这项工作做得对不对，因为每种任务对“做对”的定义不同。
en: as a code reviewer or an eval grader. Now, the hard part for us is that it's one model, and it has to grade every kind of agent that we're running through it. Our customers build their own workflows with any agent and any tool in any order, so the permutations are almost infinite. So the list of jobs for the judge has to grow with it. The judge can tell whether the work looks finished, but what it can't tell is whether the work was right, because that depends on what right means for each job,

zh: 而我们对所有任务都问同一个问题。我会先讲我们检查裁判时发现了什么，再讲后来选的办法，以及各位今天就可以在自己的 Agent 上做些什么。
en: and we're asking it the same question for all of them. So here's where we're going. First, I'll talk about what we found when we checked the judge. Then, what we chose instead, and what you can do today with your own agents.

zh: 一开始我们做的是离线评测。我们从生产环境取出 500 个真实步骤，每个步骤都有裁判当时作出的决定。然后我们找了一个规模更大的前沿模型重新评判每一项，给出批准或退回。接着我们逐条人工检查样本，也检查模型给出的判断。
en: To start, we ran offline evals. We took 500 real steps from production, each with a decision that the judge had made. Then we took a larger frontier model and regraded every one of those to come back with an accept or send back. Then we hand-checked each of those samples and we checked the grades.

zh: 我们和模型意见不一致时，就按人工判断。这给 500 个步骤都配上了参考标签。结果发现，裁判只有 65% 的判断是对的，差不多像掷硬币。
en: Where we disagreed with the model, we went with our call. This gave us a reference label for all 500 steps. And it turned out the judge was right 65% of the time, so more or less a coin flip.

zh: 它批准了 118 个本该退回的步骤，超过全部批准项的四分之一。相当糟。我们把这些样本读了一遍，最常见的问题和开头那封邮件类似。Agent 报告自己做了某件事，比如发送了邮件，实际上没有任何一次工具调用做过那件事。[转写有缺漏]
en: It accepted 118 steps that it should have sent back. That's more than one in four of everything that it accepted. Pretty bad. And when we read through those, the most common problem was that, similar to the email at the start, the agent reported that it did something like send a no tool call had ever done that.

zh: 想知道裁判为什么批准，我们回到那个邮件例子，看看裁判当时拿到了什么。左边是 Agent 自己写的总结。你可以把它想成一个故事。
en: So to see why the judge had accepted it, let's go back to the email example and look at what the judge was given. On the left, you have what the agent's own summary. Think of it as like a story.

zh: 写得很流畅，语气也很自信，说邮件已经排定发送了。右边则是凭据，也就是工具的实际返回结果。里面有报错，有提示创建失败的消息，还明确要求 Agent 别编造记录。
en: It's confident, it's well-written. It says the email was scheduled. Now on the right, you have the receipts. This is the actual tool results. There are errors, failed to create messages, telling the agent not to make up the record.

zh: 裁判两样都拿到了，结果采信了故事。乍看工作做得没问题，它就批准了。类似的情况也会出现在别的裁判上。比如代码审查 Agent，可能会先看 PR 描述，再看代码差异。
en: Now the judge had both of these, and it went with the story. The work looked fine on the surface, so it accepted it. Now this isn't only our judge. You can think of a code review agent that reads the PR description before it looks at the diff.

zh: 这就是类似的问题。描述里说“我修了这个 bug，还加了测试”，Agent 接下来读代码时，就会受这句话影响。我们一开始想到的办法，是调一调裁判，把提示词写得更好。
en: It's a similar kind of problem. If the description says, I fixed the bug, added tests, the agent is going to lean on that when it reads the code. So the obvious fix at the start was to tune the judge and write a better prompt.

zh: [转写有缺漏] 这会是一项相当大的工程。我们的 Agent 会写销售邮件、更新 CRM，也会做调研。要评好这些任务，每次都得弄清用户究竟要求做什么。
en: is going to be a significant amount of work. Our agents write sales emails, update CRMs, do research. And to judge each of these well, we'd have to figure out what it was that the user was asking.

zh: 得给裁判配置每种任务适用的规则，还得一直更新规则。那基本上就相当于为每个使用场景定制一个裁判。我们后来走了另一条路，把“这个结果好吗”这种宽泛的大问题拿掉。
en: Give the judge the right rules for every kind of work and keep it all up to date. That's basically a custom judge for every use case. What we went with, we went a different direction. We stopped asking one big general question, is this good?

zh: 我们改问一小组简单的是非题。每个步骤都用同一组问题，每个问题都够具体，看凭据就可以回答。第一条路基本就是做一个永远改不完的提示词项目，第二条路只需要做几项小检查。我们用 Jev 来回答这些问题。今天大家已经听了很多 Jev 的介绍，我就简单带过。它是个专门做决策的模型，用来作判断。给在家里看直播的妈妈也解释一下……
en: And we started asking a short list of small yes or no questions. They are the same questions for every step, and each one is small enough to answer by looking at the receipts. The first option here is basically a prompt tuning project that never ends, whereas the second one is a small handful of small checks. Now, to answer those questions, we use Jev. You've heard a lot about Jev today, so I'll skip that and keep that short. It's a tight decision model, not a generative model. For mom at home watching,

zh: 我们会把这个步骤的结构化事实和一组有固定答题类型的问题发给它。问题可以是是非题，也可以从一组固定选项里选一个答案。它会为每个答案返回一个概率，一次调用就回答所有问题。
en: And we'll send it structured facts about the step and the listed type questions. A type question is a yes or no question or a choice from a fixed list of options. It sends back a probability for each answer, and it answers all the questions in one call.

zh: 我们给它四样东西。任务指令、输入、凭据，也就是每次工具调用及其成败，还有 Agent 的报告。然后让它在三个选项里选一个。批准、重做或停止。
en: We gave it four things, the instructions, the input, the receipts, meaning every tool call, and whether it was successful or failed, and the agent's report. Then we ask for one choice, which was accept, redo, or stop.

zh: 这个选择用来作决定。同时我们还问七道是非题。这七个答案会告诉我们作出判断的原因，帮助区分重做和停止。真的要重做时，这些答案还会写进给 Agent 的反馈。
en: And that choice makes the decision. But then we also ask seven yes or no questions. Those seven questions tell us the why. They decide between a redo and a stop, and they go into the feedback that the agent gets when it actually has to redo a step.

zh: 回到那个邮件例子。大模型裁判批准了它，花了大约 2.5 秒。Jev 则为各个选项给出概率。这一步是批准 0%，重做 97%，停止 3%，大概用了 0.2 秒。我们按批准的概率作决定。
en: Now, back to the email. The LLM judge accepted it, and it took about two and a half seconds. Jev gave us a probability for each option. For this step, it accepted 0%, redo 97%, and stop at 3%, and it took about a fifth of a second. We make the decision from the probability of accept.

zh: 30% 或更高就批准。5% 或更低就重做或停止。落在两者之间，说明 Jev 也拿不准，我们就交给大模型裁判。这两个阈值是用一开始那 500 条标注数据测试后选出来的。
en: At 30% or higher, we accept that. At 5% or lower, we redo or stop. And anything in between means JEV isn't sure, so we kick it to an LLM judge. We pick those cutoffs from testing the 500 labels that we had at the beginning.

zh: 为了检验这样做是不是更好，我们用了两种办法。第一种测试用离线评测里的同一批 500 个带标注的生产步骤。大约十个里有七个，Jev 足够有把握。在这些步骤里，大模型裁判批准了 82 个本该退回的步骤。这里每个红色方块代表其中一个。Jev 成功找出了 74 个。蓝色方块就是 Jev 会退回的步骤。第二种测试叫作影子模式。两个裁判都看每个步骤。
en: Now, to test whether or not this works better, we took two different routes. The first test used the same 500 production labels steps from the offline eval. Jev was confident enough in about 7 out of 10 of them. One of those steps, the L&M judge had accepted 82 that should have been sent back. Each red square here is one of those. Jev successfully caught 74 of those. The blue squares are the ones that Jev would have sent back. Now the second test is what we called shadow mode. Both judges look at every step,

zh: 但只有大模型裁判的决定生效。我们把 Jev 原本会怎么判存下来，不让它影响实际运行。这样我们收集到 37,000 条判定记录，可以拿来分析。期间有 728 个步骤明显发生了工具调用失败，大模型裁判发现 294 个，Jev 发现 623 个。开头那个虚报已排程的邮件案例也不是偶发的。同一个步骤运行了 1,081 次，Agent 几乎每次都说已安排邮件发送，大模型裁判只……
en: but only the LLM judge, that decision counts. So we saved Jev what would have done, and we don't let it affect the actual run. That gave us 37,000 decisions to mine for insights. And in that time, there were 728 steps where a tool had clearly failed. The LLM caught 294 of them. Jev caught 623. And the fake email from the beginning, it wasn't a one-off thing either. The same step ran 1,081 times, and almost every time the agent said it had scheduled an email, the LLM judge only

zh: 抓到过一次。Jev 抓到了 876 次。只要有裁判，每个步骤就都得等它判完。Jev 用时约为原来的十分之一，成本约为四十分之一。在这个规模上，差别很大。接下来怎么做？现在每一步都问同样的七个问题。我们把问题和事实一起交给 Jev，它给出批准、重做或停止。下一步我们会加上后置条件检查，按这一步调用了哪个工具来提问。工具会告诉我们这一步是什么，可以直接按已知信息来问。假设某一步调用的是……
en: caught it once. Jev caught that 876 times. When you have a judge, every step waits. Jev was 10 times faster and 40 times cheaper. At this scale, it is massive. So what's next? Right now, every step goes with the same seven questions. They go into Jev along with the facts and Jev gives us an accept, redo or stop. But next we're adding post condition checks, which are questions that depend on which tool called within the step. So we don't have to guess. We know the step up front because the tool tells us. If a step is called, let's

zh: 发送工具，我们还会问消息是否送达。要是它写入了一条记录，我们就问记录是否存在。这些问题跟原来的七个问题一起，在同一次调用里交给 Jev。那你今天就能对自己的 Agent 做什么？第一步，选一个判定任务。
en: say, a send tool, we also ask whether the message was delivered. If it wrote a record, we ask whether the record exists. And those go into Jev with the same seven questions in the same call. Now, what can you do today with your agents? First, pick one judgment.

zh: 你的系统里总有一个地方，是让大模型判断某件事做得好不好。可能是审代码，也可能是给评测打分。选一个，把它改写成几个简单的是非题，而且这些问题可以看证据回答。第二步，把它做出来。说实话，这是容易的一步。我们用的是 Jev，问了七个问题。第三步，开影子模式。让它和你现在的裁判并行运行，暂时别让它做实际决定。
en: Somewhere in your systems, there's an LLM deciding whether or not something is good. It might be reviewing code, grading an eval. Pick one of those and rewrite it as a few simple yes or no questions that can be answered from the evidence. Second is build it. This is the easy part, honestly. We used Jev and ours was seven questions. And then the third, Shadow mode. Run it next to what you already have, but don't let it make the decisions yet.

zh: 先把结果存下来，之后就能分析。接着逐条读这些案例，看两套判定在哪些地方不一致。别想得太复杂，从一小处做起就好。我们原本一直信任自己的裁判，直到我们去量了它的表现。也量一下你们的裁判。再加一套检查，让它在影子模式里运行，看看有哪些分歧。
en: Just save it, and then you can analyze it later. Then read the cases and see where the two disagree. Don't overthink it, just start small. We had trusted our judge until we measured it. Measure yours. Run a second check, run it in shadow mode, and see where it disagrees.

zh: 你看到的结果也许会让你意外。
en: You may be surprised with what you find.
